title: Map build: sites from data, so the stadium survives npm run map
body:
West Seattle Stadium (#57) existed only as a hand edit to the generated `src/city/world/worldData.json`. Nothing in `scripts/city/` knew about it, so the next `npm run map` would have silently erased it.

- **Sites** (`scripts/city/sites/*.json`): places OpenStreetMap doesn't have, as data. Each is an ASCII grid of cells anchored by lat/lon (`l` lawn, `w` walkable + named, `W` walkable, `n` named), plus its label, paths and detail features in lat/lon. Anchored by lat/lon, a site stays put if the map's area changes; a build at another tile size refuses it.
- `build-map.mjs` draws every site after the landmarks and before the houses (so houses stay off it). Rules in `scripts/city/sites.mjs`, tested.
- The stadium's file was extracted from #57's own diff. A rebuild now reproduces the committed map exactly, stadium included. (The one other difference is a house that any fresh build drops at the edge of Dakota Place Park; the map data isn't touched in this PR.)
- Guard: `sites.test.mjs` fails if the committed map is missing a site.
- CLAUDE.md: never hand-edit `worldData.json`; add a site instead.

@exit320-stack: heads-up only. Nothing changes on the map; the stadium is just safe now. Next time something needs adding that OSM lacks, it goes in `scripts/city/sites/`.
